rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Design and measurement - HOBO-U30 probes monitored soil water content to 2 m in one flood-irrigated and one mulched-drip section from 24 May to 22 Aug 2017; monthly groundwater depth from seven monitoring wells 2014-2018 compiled (Changes in groundwater depth). Q2: Results, Changes in groundwater depth and Figure 5 - flood irrigation shows a more dramatic response to rainfall infiltration and a quicker rise of groundwater level than mulched drip irrigation; under flood irrigation at ~8 m depth groundwater rose 0.98 m one month after >300 mm monthly rainfall, whereas under mulched drip at 4-5 m it rose 0.77 m three months later and at 6 m showed no response; Figure 4 - infiltration depth and replenishment amount under rainstorm greater in flood area than mulched-drip area. Q3: two independent measurement methods - in-situ soil moisture probes (Figure 4) and groundwater observation wells (Figure 5) both indicate greater recharge response under flood irrigation. Q4: Figure 4 and Results - soil moisture content at 50, 100, 160 and 200 cm measured after each rainfall as the infiltration pathway (e.g., after the 72 mm rain, 50 cm moisture rose 7% in flood area vs 8.3% after 12 h lag in drip area; 100 cm rose 4.1% vs 0.1%; 2 m rose 1.4% after 14 days vs 0.9% after 19 days). Q6: Changes in groundwater depth / Figure 5 - effect reported at district scale using seven wells across Horqin Left Wing Middle Banner (four in mulched-drip area, three in flood area) over 2014-2018. Q7: Results - soil moisture at 100 cm and below in the mulched-drip area rises only when rainfall reaches 72 mm; groundwater level rises only when heavy monthly rainfall (>300 mm) occurs and response disappears once groundwater depth exceeds ~6 m (drip) or ~8 m for small rains (flood); authors state recharge effect is significantly weakened as groundwater level drops. Q8: Changes in groundwater depth - authors state that due to limited research conditions only soil moisture to 2 m depth was monitored while groundwater depth everywhere exceeded 3 m.
rows.notes: Study compares flood irrigation with mulched drip irrigation (drip under plastic mulch), treated here as the drip technology in the passage; the mulch component is part of the drip system tested, so not marked as a technology mismatch, though the mulch impermeability is identified by the authors as a key reason for reduced rainfall infiltration. The study's own result concerns rainfall-infiltration recharge response, not direct measurement of irrigation return flow; the 'return flow' mechanism in the passage is asserted by the authors (no return water under drip), not measured. Well comparison is confounded by differing groundwater depths and locations between the two irrigation areas (one site, one season for soil moisture). No dispersion measures reported; all values are single point estimates.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single observation point for soil moisture (one season, 2017) plus seven wells in one county; no statistics or uncertainty reported.
